items.title: fraction-score-hierarchy
items.claim: In Image #8, HasanAbi’s score has a vertically stacked half-point fraction that extends below the whole number, while Asmongold’s zero remains a compact single-line numeral.
items.reason: The uneven score shapes make the scoreboard harder to scan at a glance during a two-thumb fight.
items.suggest: Use a compact typographic half glyph beside the whole number, and align both players’ scores within the same visual band while preserving readable text.

items.title: round-intro-copy-overload
items.claim: In Image #2, the dark panel combines an opponent scouting sentence with a multi-line control explanation between the matchup heading and the Techniques button.
items.reason: The player must separate tactical advice from basic instructions before reaching the prominent Fight action.
items.suggest: Keep one short opponent tip on the round card, move the detailed input explanation into Techniques, and retain a concise first-to-two rule beside Fight.

items.title: direction-legend-decoding
items.claim: In Image #3, the instruction strip compresses stance and technique mappings into two adjacent text groups, including 'back · reverse' and 'forward · punch', while the sticks themselves show direction marks without action labels.
items.reason: A newcomer has to repeatedly translate the legend into thumb directions instead of recognizing the desired action directly on the control.
items.suggest: Place short action labels around each stick’s corresponding directions, with a distinct treatment for stance versus technique, and remove the duplicated instruction strip once that mapping is readable.

items.title: scoring-banner-dominance
items.claim: In Image #20, the Waza-ari announcement occupies a broad dark band above the fighters, with the award word substantially more prominent than either the scoring technique or the updated half-point score.
items.reason: The spectacle communicates that something happened more strongly than what the player earned and which move earned it.
items.suggest: Use a more compact award card that groups 'Half point', the fighter name, and 'Lunge Punch', leaving more of the dojo visible and giving the updated score a coordinated emphasis.

items.title: result-lettering-shadow-weight
items.claim: In Image #18, the winner heading and result numerals have conspicuous dark offset shadows and outlined edges, whereas the Rematch label uses clean, flat lettering.
items.reason: The competing text treatments make the result screen feel less cohesive, and the large shadows add visual clutter to its most important message.
items.suggest: Give the winner heading and score the same crisp typographic family as the action button, retaining a restrained gold highlight and a softer, smaller shadow for separation.
